questions.stem: A user needs to transfer a 6 GB video file from a Windows laptop to a MacBook using a USB flash drive. Which filesystem should the flash drive be formatted with?
questions.explanation: exFAT is cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS) and supports files larger than 4 GB. It was designed by Microsoft specifically for flash drives.
questions.trap: FAT32 is also cross-platform but caps individual files at 4 GB, so a 6 GB video will not fit.

questions.stem: Which workstation OS is built on the Linux kernel but designed so most applications run inside a browser?
questions.explanation: Chrome OS was built by Google on the Linux kernel, and most applications run inside the Chrome browser.
questions.trap: Android is also Linux-based but is a mobile OS, not a workstation OS.

questions.stem: A developer wants to build iOS apps. Which operating system must they develop on?

choices.text: Any OS that supports the Apple SDK

questions.explanation: Apple's Software Developer's Kit for iOS, iPadOS, and macOS apps runs only on macOS. Apps must also be approved by Apple before publication in the App Store.
questions.trap: Android apps CAN be developed on Windows, macOS, or Linux. iOS cannot.

questions.stem: A company needs the lowest possible licensing cost for desktops but is fine handling support themselves. Which OS best fits?
questions.explanation: Linux is free with no licensing fees. The company can rely on the community for support since they have stated they will handle support themselves.
questions.trap: macOS has no per-seat OS license fee either, but it requires Apple hardware, which has a higher initial cost. The question is about the lowest total cost when support is self-managed.

questions.stem: Which filesystem provides self-healing, large-array support, and RAID-like features and is primarily intended for Windows Server environments?
questions.explanation: ReFS (Resilient File System) is Microsoft's NTFS successor, designed for large arrays with self-healing and RAID-like features. It first appeared in Server 2012.
questions.trap: XFS has similar large-array characteristics but is a Linux filesystem, not Windows. NTFS is the Windows default but does not have the self-healing or RAID-like features described.

questions.stem: A technician receives a phone that runs an OS based on Linux, sold by multiple manufacturers, with apps distributed through Google Play and third-party stores. Which OS is on the phone?
questions.explanation: Android is open source, Linux-based, supported by many hardware manufacturers, and is distributed via Google Play plus third-party stores.
questions.trap: iOS and iPadOS only run on Apple hardware and only distribute through Apple's App Store. Chrome OS is for desktops/laptops, not phones.

questions.stem: Match each filesystem to the OS or device class it is most strongly associated with.
questions.explanation: Each pair reflects the default or primary use case shown in the 1.1 objective.
questions.trap: APFS is the default for modern macOS only; older macOS used HFS+ (not on this exam). Don't pick APFS for general Linux storage even though both are modern.

questions.stem: Which statements about macOS are TRUE? Select all that apply.

choices.text: It runs only on Apple-manufactured hardware.
It tends to have higher initial hardware cost than Windows machines.
It has more third-party industry support than Windows.

questions.explanation: macOS runs exclusively on Apple hardware (a) and that hardware tends to cost more upfront (c). macOS is closed source. Windows has more third-party industry support because of its larger user base.
questions.trap: Choosing (d) because of macOS's perceived quality. Industry support volume follows market share, and Windows has the larger share.
